about.title: Westminster Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: A hospital stay or clinic visit is supposed to make things better. When it doesn't — because a diagnosis was missed, a medication was mixed up, or a surgeon hurried through a step — the people of Westminster are left sorting out what happened and who answers for it. California's MICRA rules give you one year from the date you discovered the harm to file, and never more than three years from the injury itself. Before a lawsuit, a 90-day notice has to go to the provider. And a doctor's opinion is nearly always needed to show that care fell below the accepted standard, because a disappointing result on its own is not malpractice. Westminster residents, roughly 92,000 across this Orange County city, receive care at a range of hospitals, urgent-care clinics, and specialty practices in and around town. LawProactive is not a law firm; we are a free service that puts you in touch with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Westminster Patients Turn to LawProactive

items.title: The clock is shorter than people expect
items.desc: MICRA generally allows one year from discovery and no more than three years from the injury. An attorney can pin down which date applies to you before the window closes.

items.title: The 90-day notice is handled correctly
items.desc: California requires notice to the provider before a malpractice suit is filed. The attorneys in our network know this step and build it into the timeline from the start.

items.title: Expert review comes first, not last
items.desc: A qualified medical expert is almost always needed to show the standard of care was breached, and non-economic damages are capped at an amount that rises each year. Your attorney evaluates both early so you know what you are dealing with.

items.question: I was treated after a collision on Beach Boulevard and the ER missed a fracture. Is that malpractice?
items.answer: It might be, but only if a reasonably careful emergency physician would have caught the fracture under the same circumstances. Westminster saw 112 people injured in traffic collisions in 2025, and many of them passed through local emergency rooms, so this scenario is not unusual. An attorney will typically have a medical expert review your imaging and chart before deciding whether a claim is viable.

items.question: My surgery didn't go the way I hoped. Do I have a case?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Under California law, a poor result on its own is not malpractice; there has to be a departure from accepted medical practice that caused the harm. An independent attorney can look at your records and tell you honestly whether that line was crossed.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge me anything, and are you the ones handling the case?
items.answer: We are not a law firm and we do not handle cases ourselves. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney in Westminster who takes malpractice matters on contingency. That means there is no fee unless there is a recovery.
